curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42107-1-1.pdf (one book, 128 pages; the motorcycle and its paddock stand are steps 1-209, pages 4-119, and pages 120-121 show the functions)

functions.does: The grey gear lever on the gearbox's right side picks neutral, first or second gear: it turns the selector shaft, whose orange rotary catch slides the driving ring between the two clutch gears.
functions.source: book: steps 37-39 (the selector shaft, rotary catch and lever; the 1:1 inset), steps 40-50 (the gearbox), pages 54-55 (positions N, 1 and 2 with arrows), page 121 bottom inset

functions.does: In first or second gear, turning the rear wheel runs the V4 engine: the chain from the rear sprocket drives the output shaft at the swing arm's pivot, which drives the gearbox and then the crankshaft, pumping the four pistons up and down. Second gear turns the engine at a different speed from first.
functions.source: book: steps 40-60 (gearbox and engine: crankshaft, rods and four yellow pistons), step 97 (the output shaft and sprocket), steps 125-130 (rear wheel and chain), page 121 bottom inset
functions.note: needs the gear lever in 1 or 2 first; how far to turn it isn't known, so there's no `first` yet. In neutral the rear wheel and output shaft turn but the engine stays still

functions.does: The rear wheel rides on the swing arm, which pivots on the gearbox's output shaft; the shock absorber between the swing arm's linkage and the frame lets the rear wheel rise and fall.
functions.source: book: steps 77-97 (swing arm, shock and linkage), page 120 bottom-left inset (arrow at the rear wheel)
functions.note: how far the arm can swing is set by the shock absorber's travel

functions.does: The rear shock absorber's spring pushes the rear wheel back down.
functions.skip: a spring only matters under gravity or force

functions.does: The handlebars steer: they turn the front fork with the front wheel on the steering head.
functions.source: book: steps 116-124 (fork, wheel and steering head), page 120 bottom-right inset (arrow at the front wheel)
functions.note: inferred: which parts are the handlebars (the two axles with stops, p340 and p351, either side of the top yoke)

functions.does: The front fork's two gold legs are shock absorbers: they shorten so the front wheel can rise.
functions.source: book: step 116 (the gold shock absorbers), page 120 bottom-left inset (arrow at the front wheel)
functions.note: inferred: the fork's lower ends (p408, p419) as the sliding parts; the gold shocks are p371 and p376 65151-f1, a part the LDraw library doesn't have

functions.does: The front wheel rolls freely on its axle between the fork legs.
The red paddock stand lifts the rear: pushing its handle down rocks it on its small wheels, and its front arms raise the rear wheel off the ground by pins under the swing arm.
functions.source: book: page 121 top inset (arrow up from the stand's pin to the swing arm); the stand is the stand submodel
functions.note: inferred: which part is the handle and how the stand rocks; the book only shows the lifted rear

functions.does: The side fairings come off to show the engine and gearbox.
functions.note: not a control: the fairings just unclip

questions.question: Which parts are the handlebars and the stand's handle?
